questions: Who creates and owns the two m_hViewModel handles, their models, sequences and active-weapon association?
Which server boundary commits a ranged shot and reload transaction, and what role does the model event play?

relationships.evidence: weapon update resolves its selected slot and companion slot 1
event mode invokes the ranged shot virtual
reload completion invokes the ammunition transaction

findings.fact: The player owns two independent server viewmodel entities in m_hViewModel[2], while the active weapon selects which slot receives its model and drives matching sequence and playback-rate writes on both slots.
findings.evidence: player_create_viewmodel 0x1015d6d0 creates class viewmodel and stores its EHANDLE at player+0x2308+slot*4; weapon_update_viewmodels 0x102532a0 resolves the selected slot and slot 1 separately and writes model, sequence and playback rate on each.
findings.consequence: Hands and weapon are not one combined model or one mesh component; a reproduction needs two visual instances synchronized by one semantic intent.

findings.fact: A server animation event is a routing trigger, not the gameplay shot transaction; ranged weapon logic commits the shot after the event re-enters mode dispatch.
findings.evidence: ranged_operator_handle_anim_event 0x10238160 routes 3030..3044 to ranged_mode_dispatch 0x102383b0, whose event arm invokes ranged_shot_commit 0x102387b0; that body clamps due shots, spends Ammo_Cost and constructs the fire packet.
findings.consequence: A client viewmodel event and muzzle flash cannot own ammunition or damage authority.
